title: Accept 20000488: Robin half-space perturbations: a credited dimension-dependent answer to AIM Problem 1.4
body:
## Accepted result and published preprint

**Robin half-space perturbations: a credited dimension-dependent answer to AIM Problem 1.4**, Alec Kriebel. Published paper and verification package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23431279 (https://zenodo.org/records/23431279).

A credited negative answer to the literal dimension-unrestricted AIM Problem 1.4. A specified nonzero smooth graph f=h/100 in R4 has spectrum [-1,infinity) at attractive Robin strength beta=1. Every connected smooth nontrivial compact half-space perturbation in ambient dimensions two and three binds below -beta^2 for every beta>0, including overhangs and compact boundary components. All compact W1,infinity graphs in dimensions at least four have absence at sufficiently weak strength depending on the graph. Exner-Minakov are credited for planar binding AND the exponential/Stokes normal-defect mechanism. Graph absence and the explicit example are also credited corollaries of Hoang-Hundertmark-Richter-Vugalter published Theorem A.6 through a complete bounded H1 geometric and Fourier bridge; Frank-Laptev flat Robin/relativistic duality, standard criticality/capacity and classical Hardy are credited. The paper includes a self-contained Hardy-trace proof and an exact earlier-theorem count certificate N<1/240. No all-strength absence for one fixed nonzero graph, general higher-dimensional nongraph classification or embedded-eigenvalue exclusion is asserted. Historical priority of exact remaining geometric formulations, novelty, worldwide open status and independent discovery remain UNKNOWN. Extensive AI assistance in solving, verification, source comparison, coding and writing. Unrefereed; no human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification.

## Accepted scope and review

Every nontrivial connected smooth compact half-space perturbation binds at every attractive β in dimensions 2,3; compact Lipschitz graphs in dimensions≥4 have weak-coupling spectrum [-β²,∞); explicit f=h/100, n=4,β=1 disproves dimension-unrestricted universal binding.

No gap asserted in dimension-unrestricted negative answer. Source dimension interpretation must be checked; separate dimension-3 reading is also covered by positive theorem. No all-coupling graph absence/nongraph higher-dimensional classification or embedded-eigenvalue exclusion claimed.

The result is accepted at the exact audited head `5e23f0c801d23976830657d2eef2b32bdc7da05a`. 3 fresh independent complete AI whole-package reviews were completed, with the final review finding zero actionable issues. Subsequent bounded administrative adoption is recorded in the current external ROOT final seal; earlier status/counter/hold fields remain dated history. Prior mathematical results and proof dependencies are credited. Historical novelty and worldwide current openness are unestablished. AI tools were used extensively; this is an unrefereed preprint, without conventional human peer review or formal proof certification.

The repository Zenodo uploader verified the exact reviewed metadata and PDF/support bytes. The Google Workspace CLI recorded the DOI/details in the requested tracker with exact read-back. No GitHub release is created. Current audit and publication receipts: `audits/pr1085_20000488`.

## Accepted full negative answer, attempt 1/5

AIM Problem 1.4, Shape optimization with surface interactions; corpus 20000488 / AIM-ANALYSIS-0020, rank 1269. The question is dimension-unrestricted. A genuine nonzero smooth compact graph in R4 at attractive Robin coupling beta=1 has spectrum [-1,infinity), disproving the universal claim of binding below the flat threshold. Both domain and boundary are connected.

The complete analytic report also proves all-coupling binding for every nontrivial connected smooth compact half-space perturbation in n=2,3, including overhangs and compact additional boundary components. In n>=4 every compact Lipschitz graph has weak-coupling absence below threshold. The essential-spectrum proof, form-core details, global boundary-defect identity, capacity test, self-contained Hardy–trace estimate, all-function bound and exact f=h/100 counterexample are retained in full.

The full dimension-unrestricted universal question is resolved negatively. No classification of arbitrary nongraph domains in n>=4, all-coupling absence, exclusion of embedded eigenvalues, or literature novelty is claimed. Exner–Minakov receive credit for the standard planar result; strong-coupling, magnetic-operator and historical talk statements retain their precise distinctions.
